solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spray paint with a sheen

indicators.note: to spray is to scatter in all directions, so the letters of the next words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for a decorator: apply paint from an aerosol so the finish has a gloss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' looks like an instruction to the decorator, but it rearranges PAINT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is the soft lustre that old wood or bronze acquires, a kind of surface gloss.

clue.text: C in Cook?

parts.note: the letter C begins the word Cook, so it is the first one; also Alastair Cook went in first to bat for England

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a letter inside a surname or a kitchen word.
explanation.walkthrough: Alastair Cook was England's first-wicket batsman at the time; in cricket the batsman who goes in first is called by this name. The letter C also starts the word Cook.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of a word starts it off, just as a batsman going in first starts an innings.

clue.text: Cliff hit Norway in a nostalgic tour that's rocking

indicators.note: the letter for Norway goes inside the rearranged letters
rocking means swaying about, so the letters of the preceding phrase are shaken into a new order

parts.note: N is the international vehicle registration for Norway

explanation.surface: Cliff Richard sets off on a nostalgia tour of Norway with plenty of rock and roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' rearranges A NOSTALGIC TOUR, and 'in' puts N among those letters. Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard's song of this title was the UK's 1968 Eurovision entry and a number-one single.

clue.text: Handicap race held in centre of Epsom? True/false

indicators.note: the race is held inside the following letters, enclosed by them
the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter
false here means not genuine, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A racing tipster asks whether a handicap race at Epsom is genuine or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' reorders the word true into UTER, and 'held in' puts the race inside the centre letter plus those. Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment is a handicap, and repeating the opening sounds of words is a common one.

clue.text: Wee hiking boot with a fashionable crepe sole rounding off daring outfit

indicators.note: the last piece rounds off, or finishes, the whole answer

parts.note: wee is a childish word for urine, as is pee

indicators.note: fashionable means made into a new style, so the letters of hiking boot and a are refashioned
the sole of a word is its bottom letter, here the last one

explanation.surface: A tiny hiking boot with a trendy crepe sole as the final touch to a bold outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges HIKING BOOT A into KABOONIGHTI; 'sole' takes the last letter of crepe, E, which 'rounding off' puts at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short, revealing nightdress, so a racy piece of clothing for the bedroom.

clue.text: Multilingual college's German student's almost excessive

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a kind of British college
L is the learner plate on a British student driver's car

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite finished, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A college's German student is almost too good at languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims OTT to OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks many languages is a polyglot; the adjective describes such speech or writing.

clue.text: Deputised in charge of teaching

parts.note: someone who deputised did act in another's place

explanation.surface: A stand-in placed in charge of the teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deputised' is read as two words, DID ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Didactic means intended to instruct, so relating to teaching.

clue.text: Standard supporter of 10 player

definitions.meaning: a lamp standard is an upright pole carrying a street light
George Formby, the ukulele player, sang about leaning on one of these

explanation.surface: A routine backer of a footballer wearing the number 10 shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby was a British comedian whose famous song was 'Leaning on a Lamp-post'; 10 refers to the ukulele answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A street-light post is called a standard, and it held up Formby in his song.

clue.text: Concerned with sexual desire, solicitor expertly reviewed evidence in case

indicators.note: reviewed is read as viewed again backwards, so the letters run in reverse
the letters are on show inside the casing of the words, held within them

explanation.surface: In a sex case, a solicitor expertly goes over the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evidence in case' shows letters inside SOLICITOR EXPERTLY; 'reviewed' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic describes things arousing or relating to sexual desire.

clue.text: 8 leaner got lots more pleasure when he was playing with his wig half off

definitions.text: 8 leaner got lots more pleasure when he was playing with his

indicators.note: half the letters of the word are taken off its front

parts.note: a peruke is an old word for a periwig

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of George Formby enjoying himself more while his wig slipped.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby, the lamppost leaner, was a British comic singer famous for 'With My Little Ukulele in My Hand', a song full of innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Formby's instrument was the ukulele, often shortened to this three-letter form.

clue.text: Rotten timing combined with delayed start and latish finish in pitch darkness

indicators.note: rotten means decayed or corrupted, so the letters are spoilt into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter
the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A late start and slightly late finish make poor timing for a game played in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' rearranges TIMING with D (start of delayed) and H (finish of latish).
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the night is the darkest hour, and 'dark as midnight' means pitch black.

clue.text: Island home that could be remote

parts.note: a key is a low-lying island, as in the Florida Keys
pad is informal for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: A house on an island that might be far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remote' suggests isolation but means a television remote control.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote control is one example of a pad of buttons for entering commands.

clue.text: Match strength with a nubile state

parts.note: a match is a marriage, as in a good match
ability is a strength or talent

explanation.surface: A dating advert pairing physical strength with youthful charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile means of an age or condition suitable for wedlock, so this is that condition.

clue.text: See 19
Cold and sour, lacking Southern openness

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Someone cold and sour, without any warm southern frankness.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness, being open and honest in speech.

clue.text: Slippery character the centre of attraction in an archetypal Essex girl's Japanese car

indicators.note: the centre of a ten-letter word is its fifth and sixth letters
the stereotypical Essex accent drops the h at the start of words

parts.note: Honda is a Japanese car maker

explanation.surface: The stereotypical Essex girl's flashy Japanese car is the centre of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives AC; the 'archetypal Essex girl' drops her aitches, so HONDA becomes ONDA. Essex is a county east of London with a brash stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge South American snake is a slippery creature, and character can mean a creature.

clue.text: Spread rumour about international crime chief getting overturned judgement

indicators.note: in a down light, overturned means turned upside down, so the letters run in reverse
about means surrounding the next letters

parts.note: noised means spread as rumour, as in noised abroad

indicators.note: the chief letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: Gossip about an international crime boss whose conviction was quashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and C inside NOISED, giving NOISICED; 'overturned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision is a judgement, the ruling a court or referee gives.

clue.text: Various broths including cold soup

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the letter goes inside
various means of different kinds, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A menu offering several broths, one of them a chilled soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges BROTHS, and 'including' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is a beetroot-based soup from Eastern Europe, often served chilled.

clue.text: Second aperitif before the middle of brunch and it's downhill all the way

parts.note: kir is a French aperitif of white wine and cassis

indicators.note: the middle of a six-letter word is its third and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Another drink before brunch, after which everything goes downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downhill all the way' sounds like decline but literally describes a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski slope runs entirely downward for skiers, so this phrase describes one exactly.

clue.text: Cape has marks in fabric — not fine linen

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the shortened word
not here means removing a letter from the word

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A cape stained with marks on coarse cloth rather than fine linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fine' drops F from FABRIC, leaving ABRIC, and 'in' puts M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white linen or cotton cloth.

clue.text: Drunk can banish a claim for characteristically riotous behaviour

indicators.note: drunk means intoxicated and unsteady, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunk can make a fake claim to get rid of a charge for rowdy conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges CAN BANISH A CLAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus was the god of wine, and his festivals were by repute drunken and wild orgies.

clue.text: Aura of major star in the ascendant having secured leads in international movie blockbusters

indicators.note: having secured means holding the following letters inside
in a down light, ascending means reading upward, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: the sun is our major star

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A rising film star surrounded by glamour after landing leading roles in big international movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the ascendant' turns the star round to NUS in this down light; 'having secured' means it wraps the three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a halo or glow of light around a holy figure, an aura.

clue.text: Extremely filthy place without lavatory, as 5 is likely to be

indicators.note: without means outside, so the filthy place wraps round the lavatory

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, an extremely dirty place
can is slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A disgusting dump with no toilet, the sort of place a skimpy nightie belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 5 is the peekaboo nightie.
explanation.definitionFit: A revealing nightdress is skimpy, using little fabric.

clue.text: No one's born a criminal — this anomaly's the result of nurture

definitions.text: this anomaly's the result of nurture

indicators.note: criminal means wrong and corrupt, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: one's is I'S, one being I

explanation.surface: A claim in the nature versus nurture debate: no one is born a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges NO, I'S, B and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree kept tiny by careful pruning, so its dwarf form comes from cultivation.

clue.text: Arty type half constricted by convention ultimately

indicators.note: the half is held by the constricting snake, inside it

parts.note: a boa constrictor is the snake that constricts
hemi is a Greek prefix meaning half

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: An artistic type only partly bound by convention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constricted by' is read as held inside a BOA (constrictor), giving BOHEMIA; 'ultimately' adds N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian is an unconventional artistic person living a free life.

clue.text: Sounds like alternative source of power for 8, say

indicators.note: this tells the solver to take a word that is said the same way

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A homophone puzzle about another source of energy for a lamppost.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 here is not 8 across but an eight, a rowing crew of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers pull these to drive the boat, so each powers an eight.

clue.text: Communicate with a radio presenter broadcasting around one

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents radio shows

indicators.note: around means surrounding the next letter

parts.note: on means on air, broadcasting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a radio DJ while he is on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communicate with' is used of rooms that open into each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms that communicate are joined, sharing a door, so they are next to each other.

clue.text: Succinct resignation speech in city following individual lack of justice

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the individual

parts.note: I is one, an individual

indicators.note: in means the speech goes inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York City
a resignation speech at its briefest is the two words I quit

explanation.surface: A curt resignation speech by someone in the city who has suffered injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: The resignation speech is I QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross injustice or wickedness.
